title: Assisted onboarding for neighbourhood merchants
proposal: At Kaveri Pay, pilot a Kannada and Hindi assisted-onboarding flow for 600 neighbourhood merchants before changing the self-service UPI signup experience.
reasons: The pilot addressed document-upload failures observed in support tickets.
Agents could resume an incomplete application without asking merchants to restart.
Expansion required activation above 65% and no increase in KYC rejection rate for four consecutive weeks.
impact: Thirty-day activation rose from 48% to 69% across 600 pilot merchants; KYC rejection stayed at 4%.

title: Support chatbot with a human escalation queue
proposal: Use a chatbot for merchant payment-status and refund questions, with human escalation for unresolved cases.
reasons: The bot answered routine payment-status questions consistently.
Refund exceptions needed account context that the bot could not access.
Escalations entered the general queue without carrying the conversation transcript, forcing merchants to repeat their issue.
impact: Routine ticket volume fell 24%, but refund-case resolution rose from 9 to 14 hours during the eight-week pilot.

title: Annual cloud commitment ahead of measured demand
proposal: Sign a twelve-month cloud compute commitment based on the sales team's projected doubling of merchant transaction traffic.
reasons: The demand forecast counted signed partners before their technical integrations were complete.
The commitment could not be transferred to the database capacity that became the actual bottleneck.
Finance had no monthly utilisation checkpoint before the purchase.
impact: Committed compute averaged 57% utilisation; ₹16 lakh of prepaid capacity went unused over twelve months.

title: SMS provider switch
proposal: Move merchant login OTP messages to a cheaper SMS provider to reduce per-message costs by 22%.
reasons: Acceptance tests covered Bengaluru and Mumbai but did not sample tier-2 carrier routes.
The cheaper provider's OTP delivery fell to 91% in tier-2 cities.
The provider could not restore the affected routes within the agreed recovery window; Kaveri Pay reverted after three weeks.
impact: OTP delivery fell to 91% in tier-2 cities; login-related support tickets rose 34%; the switch was reverted after three weeks.

title: Project Lotus
proposal: In Q3 2023, remove Kaveri Pay's free merchant tier and require small merchants to migrate to a paid monthly plan.
reasons: Support lacked migration capacity to help small merchants understand the paid plan and move their accounts.
A competitor ran a free-tier campaign in the same month as the migration.
The rollout removed the free tier without a staged migration path for low-volume merchants.
impact: Merchant churn reached 31% in six weeks after the free tier was removed.

title: Automated settlement reconciliation
proposal: Automate daily settlement reconciliation using bank statement imports and a queue for unmatched transactions.
reasons: Exact-reference matches removed repetitive spreadsheet work.
Two bank partners changed statement formats without notice.
The exception queue had no named owner on weekends, delaying investigation of unmatched settlements.
impact: Automatic matching reached 88% and saved 23 staff-hours weekly; weekend exceptions still took a median 31 hours to resolve.

title: Instant Settlement
proposal: Offer instant merchant settlement for eligible payment flows before completing a fraud-ops review.
reasons: The launch proceeded without a fraud-ops review.
Settlement eligibility relied on account age without transaction-velocity controls.
Fraud operations could not review suspicious bursts before funds were released.
impact: Month-one chargebacks reached ₹38 lakh; the Instant Settlement launch was rolled back.

title: QR soundbox rollout
proposal: Pilot QR soundboxes with 400 merchants in Mysuru, the only pilot city, and expand to five further cities only after measurable reliability and support gates pass.
reasons: Expansion required payment-alert delivery of at least 99.5%, weekly active usage of at least 80%, and no more than 5 support tickets per 100 devices per week for four consecutive weeks.
The Mysuru pilot reached 99.7% alert delivery, 86% weekly active usage, and 3 tickets per 100 devices per week.
A local replacement partner and trained support agents were in place before each new city opened.
impact: The rollout grew from 400 devices in Mysuru to 3,200 across six cities in five months; payment-confirmation disputes fell 28% among participating merchants.

title: Opt-in paid merchant analytics pilot
proposal: Test a paid analytics add-on with 300 established merchants while preserving their existing payment plan and offering a thirty-day trial.
reasons: Merchants opted in after seeing an example report using their own sales categories.
Support received a migration guide and reserved onboarding slots before invitations went out.
The pilot retained the existing payment plan and required trial cancellation to take no more than two clicks.
impact: Of 300 invited merchants, 96 became paying analytics users after the trial; ninety-day retention of those subscribers was 91%.

title: Unified merchant support console
proposal: Bring payment status, merchant account history, and prior support conversations into a read-only support console for all 26 support agents.
reasons: Agents helped design the console around the three most common investigation tasks.
Read-only access and role-based masking limited accidental changes and unnecessary exposure of merchant data.
A two-week shadow rollout verified that displayed payment status matched the source systems.
impact: Median ticket handling time fell from 11 to 7 minutes; repeat contacts within seven days fell from 19% to 12% over eight weeks.

title: Automatic merchant holds for unusual transaction bursts
proposal: Automatically place temporary settlement holds on merchant accounts with unusually high transaction velocity.
reasons: The velocity rule caught repeated small-value transactions used in suspected abuse.
Thresholds were calibrated on weekday trading and incorrectly flagged legitimate festival stalls.
The appeals queue lacked a same-day service target during the first month.
impact: Confirmed fraud losses fell 21% in the eight-week pilot, but 7% of held accounts were legitimate merchants and median appeal resolution was 19 hours.

title: Subscription invoicing for small merchants
proposal: Launch recurring invoice templates for all merchants after interviewing ten large tuition centres.
reasons: Research covered larger tuition centres whose billing needs differed from neighbourhood shops.
The default monthly billing workflow did not fit merchants who collected irregular instalments.
The team shipped the full editor before testing whether merchants would send a second invoice.
impact: Only 8% of 2,000 invited merchants sent an invoice, and 2% sent a second invoice within sixty days; planned expansion was cancelled.

title: Regional-language support scheduling
proposal: Pilot Kannada and Telugu support coverage during merchant peak hours, using ticket arrival data to set staffing rather than adding uniform all-day shifts.
reasons: Ticket analysis identified an evening peak that the existing shift pattern did not cover.
Bilingual agents reviewed translated help articles before the pilot.
Expansion required first response under ten minutes and no worsening of the English-language queue for six weeks.
impact: Median first response in the pilot queues fell from 27 to 8 minutes; merchant satisfaction rose from 74% to 86% with two additional evening shifts.

title: Payments release gates with staffed rollback ownership
proposal: Require a named on-call owner, a tested rollback, and a 5% merchant canary before expanding changes to the payment routing service.
reasons: The canary gate stopped expansion if payment success dropped by more than 0.3 percentage points for ten minutes.
Support and payments operations received the rollout window before deployment.
Two canaries were rolled back within the pilot gate; neither reached the full merchant population.
impact: Across 18 releases over twelve weeks, median rollback time fell from 26 to 7 minutes and customer-visible release incidents fell from 5 in the prior quarter to 1.
